title: Embed/Rerank protocol stability and client hints
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: Multiple legacy clients call our embeddings and rerank endpoints with differing expectations for pagination (offsets, page tokens, link headers) and error semantics (500 vs 429 vs transient 503). New unified endpoints (embeddings-v2 + rerank-v2) expose streaming and structured outputs which complicate parity behavior for non-streaming legacy callers. This ticket defines the engineering spec for a compatibility shim that provides stable cursor semantics, canonical error mapping, and client-visible retry hints without regressing modern clients.

Goals:
- Define canonical cursor format and lifecycle (opaque token that encodes server generation, model variant, and a checksum; supports tombstones for removed items).
- Provide deterministic error mappings from legacy numeric HTTP+body semantics to the new canonical codes and messages.
- Surface client retry hints (Retry-After header and X-Redwood-Retry-Hint for backoff/fuzz), and include idempotency guidance for rerank jobs.
- Ensure streaming responses (when enabled) include an initial stability envelope so clients can fall back to polling with cursors.
- Avoid double-counting tokens/charges for compatibility adapter and ensure billing telemetry remains accurate.

Proposed solution (engineering notes):
1) Cursor contract: base64(urlsafe) token with prefix v1c|<unix_ts>|<nonce>|<model_tag>|<crc8>. Server validates prefix and ts window (48h) to allow rolling upgrades. When a result set includes removed items the cursor includes a tombstone flag (T) and a tombstone-list hash. Legacy clients that expect page numbers will receive Link headers with rel=next/prev mapping to our cursor tokens.
2) Error mapping: map legacy 500->500 (internal), 503 transient->429 if caused by rate or queue length, include structured error field "compat_code" (e.g., EMBED_RATE_LIMIT, RERANK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED). For structured-output clients, include an additional field `legacy_hint` in the top-level error JSON for human-readable migration steps.
3) Retry hints: always set Retry-After for 429/503; for fine-grained guidance add X-Redwood-Retry-Hint: "backoff=exponential;min=200;max=5000;jitter=0.25". Clients can ignore this but SDKs will use it by default.
4) Streaming fallback: streaming first chunk will include a "compatibility_envelope" object (when compatibility_mode header is present) that contains the canonical cursor for the remainder of the result set and a stable checksum. If a client disconnects mid-stream they can resume using the envelope cursor.
5) Adapter: implement a compatibility-layer microservice (compat-proxy) that translates legacy client requests to the new endpoints. It will: normalize pagination params, translate legacy API keys to current tokens, perform error remapping, and emit provenance headers for billing. This proxy will run in host mode for hosted customers and as a shim in Private deployments when compatibility_mode=true.

Acceptance criteria (tests and telemetry):
- Unit tests for cursor generation/validation and tombstone handling.
- Integration tests mapping 8 legacy error cases to canonical outputs.
- E2E test: legacy client pagination test reproducing previous offsets-based navigation and Link header behavior.
- Load test validating proxy adds <5ms median latency and does not increase token billing by more than 0.5%.
- Dashboards: new charts for compatibility-requests, error-mapping counts, proxy latency, and retry loops.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Adding an adapter adds operational complexity and a small latency tax. We limit risk by optimizing the proxy path and shipping heuristics to bypass the proxy when clients supply a modern accept header.
- Cursor complexity (including tombstones) increases token size and parsing surface. We mitigate by keeping tokens compact and validating early at edge.
- Exposing Retry-Hint could have clients rely on server timing; SDKs will enforce sane caps.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (shadow): launch compat-proxy in shadow mode routing 1% of legacy traffic, collect telemetry and run canary tests (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (opt-in): add a header X-Redwood-Compat: accept-always for customer opt-in, 25% traffic for 1 week.
- Phase 3 (default): flip compat-proxy on for all legacy keys with a 72-hour monitoring window and automatic rollback triggers for error spikes.

Monitoring & Playbooks:
- Create alert when mapped 429/503 rate exceeds baseline by 30% for 10m.
- Build a troubleshooting runbook: how to correlate a legacy client id to the compat-proxy trace, how to regen cursors, and how to expedite customer migration.

Docs & SDKs:
- PM & Docs to publish migration guide showing cursor examples, error mappings, and recommended backoff.
- SDK patches to transparently consume Retry-Hint and resume from compatibility_envelope cursors.

Security and privacy notes:
- Cursor tokens do not contain PII; they encode only model tag, time, and a nonce + checksum.
- Compat-proxy must respect customer KMS settings in Private deployments.

Open questions:
- Exact tombstone list size limit (propose 512 bytes encoded).
- Whether to include explicit model-version hash in cursor to enable model-change mismatch detection (favored: yes).
